title: Fare Rules Note on Tickets Booked under Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements
content:
**Rule.** A ticket counts as booked under a Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements agreement only when all three of the following hold: it was booked through one of the tier's eligible booking channels; it carries the agreement's tour code, on a tier where the tour code is required; and it is for a traveler on the agreement's active roster on the booking date.

| Booked through an eligible channel | Tour code on the booking (tier requiring it) | Traveler on the active roster on the booking date | Booked under the agreement |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes | yes |
| yes | yes | no | no |
| yes | no | yes | no |
| no | yes | yes | no |
| any other combination with at least one "no" | | | no |

**Negotiated discount.** The negotiated discount applies to the base fare of tickets in the tier's discount-eligible fare brands: at the tier's domestic discount percentage for domestic and short-haul international itineraries, and at the tier's international discount percentage for long-haul international itineraries. It never reduces government taxes and fees on a tier where the discount does not apply to taxes.

**Allowances.** Tickets booked under the agreement also receive the change fee waiver and the corporate checked bag allowance that the Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand rules apply from the tier's figures. They may be reassigned to another traveler on the active roster on a tier that permits traveler reassignment, and their credits may pay for another roster traveler's ticket under the same agreement on a tier that permits credit pooling.

**Excluded tickets.** Crestline Basic Economy tickets, award tickets and companion tickets are never booked under an agreement.

**No combining.** The negotiated discount is not combined with any other promotional fare discount; the lower resulting fare is charged.

### Worked figures (hypothetical)

- A long-haul international ticket in a discount-eligible brand has a base fare of USD 1000.00 on a tier with an international discount of 10 percent: the base fare charged is USD 900.00, and taxes and fees are charged as filed.
- The same ticket could instead be sold under a promotional fare of USD 880.00. The two discounts are not stacked: the lower resulting fare, USD 880.00, is charged.
- A Crestline Basic Economy ticket booked through an eligible channel with the tour code, for a roster traveler, is still not booked under the agreement.
